questions.stem: A = {Pune, Mumbai} and B = {Pune, Mumbai, Nagpur}. Which statement is true?
questions.explain: Every member of A is also in B, so A is a subset of B. B has Nagpur, which A lacks, so they are not equal.

questions.stem: A cube has 3 dimensions: time, item and location. How many subsets of this set of dimensions are there, counting the empty set and the full set?
questions.explain: Each dimension is either in or out of a subset, so 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 subsets.

questions.stem: In a star schema, which table holds the numeric measures such as sales amount?
questions.explain: The fact table sits in the centre, stores the measures and links to the dimension tables by keys.

questions.stem: Which of these is a measure, a number that is added up or averaged, rather than a dimension attribute?
questions.explain: Sales amount can be summed. Category, city and month are labels used to group the facts.

questions.stem: A star schema has one fact table and 4 dimension tables. How many tables is that in total?
questions.explain: 1 fact table plus 4 dimension tables makes 5 tables.
